issues.description: Doc-only change; data shape of preview payloads is the right primitive
issues.detail: This PR is documentation for the preview_fn feature. The underlying design — typed preview payloads (JsonPreview, TablePreview, PlotlyPreview, MermaidPreview, ImagePreview, TextPreview, CustomPreview) as small data containers with content + meta — is the right shape. Each preview is a tagged union over a payload. The algorithm (rendering) follows from the data tag. That's exactly the data-dominates pattern. No structural objection.

issues.description: Closure example for data context teaches the wrong pattern
issues.detail: The 'Use closure to capture context' example captures a hardcoded sample_data list at pipeline construction time. This is not preview-of-actual-data; it is preview-of-frozen-literal. A reader will copy this pattern thinking it gives them a live preview tied to the node's real I/O, then be surprised when the preview never updates. Either show a real pattern (load the dataset by name from the catalog inside the preview_fn) or be explicit that preview_fn is decoupled from node I/O by design and closures only help with static context.

issues.description: Mermaid config example is too clever for an intro doc
issues.detail: The generate_mermaid_preview example pulls in securityLevel, nodeSpacing, rankSpacing, curve, themeVariables, and a textStyle block before the reader has a working preview. This is framework-shaped documentation: every knob shown at once. Smaller would be better — one minimal Mermaid example, then a short 'advanced: meta accepts a Mermaid config' subsection with a link. n is small; most readers will never tune wrappingWidth.

issues.description: Meta parameter is doing two unrelated jobs
issues.detail: The doc says meta serves two purposes: general metadata and rendering configuration. That is a smell worth naming. One field is a freeform dict for human context; the other is a structured config the renderer parses. Conflating them means a typo in render config silently becomes metadata, and vice versa. The doc cannot fix this — but it should at least flag that mixing the two in one meta dict is on the user, and that renderer-reserved keys (language, securityLevel, flowchart, textStyle) take precedence. Otherwise readers will collide keys.

In the Basic usage block, preview_dict = preview.to_dict() is computed and then nothing is done with it. Docs are read as code. Either drop the line or show what it is for (e.g., 'send to a frontend / write to JSON'). Small thing, but the persona test is: would a junior copy this and wonder what they missed?

issues.description: next(n for n in pipeline.nodes) is cleverness without payoff
issues.detail: training_node = next(n for n in pipeline.nodes) is just pipeline.nodes[0] dressed up, and only correct because there is exactly one node. In a doc that teaches the API, prefer the obvious form or pipeline.nodes[0], or filter by name (the node has name='train_model_node'). Teach the boring version.

'Handle errors: Wrap preview logic in try-except if needed' tells the reader nothing about what to return on failure, whether kedro swallows the exception, or whether a failed preview breaks the node run. Either specify the contract (preview_fn exceptions are caught and surfaced as X) or drop the bullet. Vague safety advice is worse than no advice.

issues.description: Release notes and tests checkboxes unchecked
issues.detail: PR checklist shows RELEASE.md not updated and tests not added. For a docs-only PR, tests-not-added is defensible, but a user-facing feature gaining documentation usually warrants a one-line RELEASE.md entry pointing at the new section. Not a code issue; a process nit.

review.summary: Doc-only PR that introduces user-facing documentation for an experimental preview_fn feature on nodes. The underlying design — small tagged payload types (Json/Table/Plotly/Mermaid/Image/Text/Custom) with content + optional meta — is the right primitive: data dominates, and the renderer follows from the data tag, so SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE applies to the API being documented. The documentation itself is mostly good but leans TOO-CLEVER in two spots: the Mermaid config example dumps every knob at once, and the closure example teaches a frozen-literal pattern that pretends to be live data. Meta is quietly doing two jobs (human metadata vs renderer config) and the doc should name that. Small nits on unused variables, cute iterator usage, and a vague error-handling bullet. Nothing blocks merge; tighten the examples and clarify the meta contract.
